symptom: `$R = call rest service get $Url (…) returns mapping M.IMM as list of M.E` over an import mapping whose root is one object passed `check` and `exec`; `mx check` reported CE0243 "The mapping used to return a value of type 'List of M.E', but now returns a value of type 'M.E'". The other five combinations built clean.
file: mdl/executor/validate_rest_mapping_result.go ValidateRestMappingResult (MDL103), called from validate_program.go next to ValidateImportMappingRange; shape from newMappingShapeResolver. Tests: validate_rest_mapping_result_test.go; fixtures mdl-examples/bug-tests/rest-mapping-list-of-object-root(.fail).mdl
cause: The REST call is the one place the author states the result's cardinality themselves (`import from mapping` infers it from the mapping), so it is the one place it can disagree with the mapping's root. The four earlier CE0243 findings were all the builder INFERRING that cardinality wrongly, so the hand-written disagreement was never recorded.
insight: **When the field-hit records for a code are all the writer's own inference going wrong, look for the one construct where the author states the value instead of the tool inferring it: that is where a script can disagree.** Measured on MxBuild 11.16.1, one microflow per case over 3 mapping roots x 2 declared results: object-rooted `as E` clean, object-rooted `as list of E` CE0243, array-rooted either clean, a root below an array either clean. Binding ONE object out of a list is a real Studio Pro pattern (PrivateCloudData.REST_GetEnvironmentByUUID), so `as E` is never judged. The shape resolver and its conservative unknowns (root path, XML, message definition, no project) already existed for MDL-MAP04, so this rule is a second consumer, not a second resolver. A first end-to-end run against a project that already held my own flows reported a reference error on every case; a project holding only the mappings gave the clean comparison, so build the comparison project from the dependencies only. Sweep: 1,322 repo .mdl files, 0 MDL103 hits. Control: stubbing the rule fails the 4 sub-tests that expect a violation; the 6-flow comparison agrees with mx check on all six.
